title: The Wick and the Ophan, In Game
eyebrow: Build plan for approval · Raids feel frightening (#386) · nothing built yet
replyPrefix: Build plan approved: fear entities, picks

short.lead: The Wick and the Ophan of Hours are modelled, animated and, as of today, import cleanly in Unity, but neither appears in a raid. This plan puts them there in three pieces, each its own pull request: the Lantern Warden turning into the Wick, the Ophan hunting, and the Ophan's artifact demand replacing the debt. Four answers were already settled on 2026-10-11 and are listed under "Already settled on 2026-10-11" in Changes; six choices are still open.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it creates and what it needs from you.
items: Both models and all fourteen clips imported and checked on 2026-10-14: compile clean, the fear import tests pass, the full editor test suite shows 250 passed and 3 skipped.
A decisions-log entry for the approved plan, and the three issues below move from planned to being built.
Your six picks, sent with "Build plan approved: fear entities".
The Lantern Warden turns into the Wick
Issue #417, The Lantern Warden turns into the Wick in raids. A guard that sees you, is hit, or is woken by a missed Somnus turns in 1.6 s on every machine, then hunts and kills on a catch.
Your picks on the order the pieces are built in, and on how many more guards stand on the ground floors.
Issue #418, The Ophan of Hours arrives in hunted raids and catches players. It arrives as the portal's clock runs low and takes artifacts or lives. A test switch forces a hunt until the quota exists.
Your picks on when the Ophan arrives, how fast it moves, and how it takes the spoils.
The artifact demand replaces the debt
Issue #419, The Ophan's artifact quota replaces the debt and the Collector. Every 3 to 5 raids it demands artifacts, shown in the Lair's ledger; unpaid, every raid is hunted.
Your picks on where artifacts are placed in the Lair and how each next demand is chosen. Later, you also approve a list of what to keep, change or drop in the debt code.

changes: new
The guard's True Form state
A one-way state on the same Lantern Warden: once turned, it stays the Wick for the rest of the raid.

Added to the guard's state set beside Patrol, Investigate, Chase, Combat, Stunned and the rest, and synced to every machine the same way the guard's alert state already is. The Wick moves faster (1.4 m/s stalking, 4.2 m/s hunting), sees only inside the light of its own fire, and kills on a catch.
A seen or hurt Lantern Warden chases and fights like any guard.
A guard that turns into the Wick and never turns back.
Being seen by a warden becomes the moment a raid goes wrong; running and hiding are the answer.

changes.alt: The Wick's design sheet and its catch clip, eight frames
changes.caption: The Wick, already modelled and animated: its catch clip, the lunge that kills.

changes: chg
What makes a Lantern Warden react
Seeing you, being hit, or a missed Somnus now turns it. Hearing still only sends it to look.
Seen or hit: it chases and fights.
Seen, hit, or woken by a missed Somnus: it turns into the Wick.
The trigger sits where the guard already confirms sight and takes damage, so there is one place that decides a turn.
chg
A Lantern Warden in human form is never killed
A hard blow to the head stuns it and knocks it down instead.
It can be killed.
It is stunned and knocked down; only its true form is dangerous.
The other guard types keep their deaths. The stun already exists and is reused.
new
The turn itself
1.6 s seen on every machine: the face splits, the lantern drops, the coat bursts, the Wick rears up.

Plays the warden's turn clip, drops the lantern at its marked moment, swaps to the Wick model at 0.9 s and plays its emerge clip. The first 0.9 s is the one moment to run. The lantern drops as a loose physics object, in the same place on every machine, and is left where it fell, dark.
Nothing; the guard just switches state.
A reveal you can see and hear from across a room.
You get a beat of warning before it hunts.

changes.alt: Eight frames of the Lantern Warden doubling over as its lantern drops
changes.caption: The first 0.9 s, already animated: the lantern drops at 0.4 s, the model swaps at 0.9 s. The Wick's emerge clip follows.

changes: new
A "guard turned" event
Published on the existing event manager when a turn starts.
The camera, sound and music listen to it. Until sounds are made for the turn, the existing player-down sting is the placeholder.
No event exists for this.
One event every view can listen to.
The fear moment lands at once on both players' screens.
new
Prefabs and animators for both creatures, built by code
Copied from the way the wizard's animator is built today, so nothing is set by hand.

The Ophan's animator goes on its rig child object, because its clips address bones from there; on the top object it would miss every bone and draw the creature a hundred times too big. Both prefabs get a small component that receives the clips' footstep, hit and lantern-drop markers, or Unity logs an error each time one fires.
The models exist only as imported files.
Ready-to-place creatures with their clips wired.
Nothing to set up by hand in the Inspector.

changes.alt: The Wick and the Ophan of Hours side by side in Unity
changes.caption: Both models as they import in Unity today, before any prefab exists.

changes: new
Hunted raids and the Ophan's arrival
On a hunted raid the Ophan arrives as the portal's clock runs low.
It uses the raid's existing portal clock. A test switch forces a hunted raid so it can be seen before the quota exists.
Raids end when the portal closes.
A creature that comes for you near the end.
Lingering for loot becomes dangerous.

changes.alt: Eight frames of the Ophan unfolding out of a point of light
changes.caption: The Ophan's arrival clip, already animated: 4 s, unfolding out of a point of light.

changes: chg
The debt and the Collector
Replaced by the Ophan's artifact demand in the third piece.
A coin debt that grows each session, and the Collector's shares.
A demand for specific artifacts every 3 to 5 raids.
Six files read the debt today. Before this piece starts you get a keep, change or drop list with file and line, and anything dropped that should return gets its own issue.
chg
The Lair's ledger book
Shows the demand, with a sketch of each wanted artifact, instead of the debt pages.
Debt pages.
The demand and its artifacts.
Built in the third piece, issue #419, The Ophan's artifact quota replaces the debt and the Collector.

changes.alt: The Lair's ledger book model, open on its tally pages
changes.caption: The ledger as it is today. The demand pages are not drawn yet; they come in the third piece.

changes: keep
Already settled on 2026-10-11
Your answers from the original handoff; nothing here needs a pick.

A catch by the Wick kills the player; death loses what they carried. More guards do stand on the ground floors; only how many is open. The dropped lantern is left where it fell, dark. The Ophan passes through walls and cannot be hidden from: carry what it asked for, or reach the portal first. Source: docs/plans/handoff-2026-10-11-true-form-and-creature.md, Part A and Part B.
keep
The event manager, the guard state machine and the downed-player system
Reused as they are.
Nothing here is replaced; the new parts plug into them.
keep
Painted fire, and no light effects on the Ophan yet
The Wick keeps its painted flames; the Ophan's glow, lightning, echoes, floor rings and pulled-back stone come later.
The fire shader and the Ophan's effects are art work outside this plan. They get their own issues when this plan is approved.
choices: order
In what order are the pieces built?
A
The Wick, then the Ophan, then the quota
The order the 2026-10-11 handoff gave. The Ophan uses a test switch for hunts until the quota exists.
B
Both creatures first in a rough version, the rules after
C
The Wick, then the quota, then the Ophan
Both creatures reach the game soonest, and each piece lands whole and tested.
guards
How many more guards stand on the ground floors, and in which Ages?
A
One more per ground-floor zone, High Medieval only
Only the Lantern Warden has a true form, and it is a High Medieval guard.
B
One more per ground-floor zone, in every Age
C
Two more per ground-floor zone, High Medieval only
Settled: more guards do stand there. One more per zone in the Age that has the Wick is the smallest change that shows the threat from the gate.
hunt
When does the Ophan arrive, and how fast does it move?
A
90 s before the portal closes, drifting at 2.5 m/s
Players walk at 5 m/s in a raid, so it closes in only on whoever lingers or is lost.
B
60 s before the portal closes, at 3.5 m/s
Shorter and faster, still under a player's 5 m/s; less time to reach the portal.
Settled: it passes through walls and cannot be hidden from. These numbers only set how close the race to the portal is.
altar
Where are artifacts placed in the Lair to pay the demand?
A
A new altar beside the Lair's portal
B
On the ledger desk, beside the book that shows the demand
C
Thrown back into the portal
One clear spot, close to where the haul comes home.
demand
How is each next demand chosen?
A
Drawn at random from the artifacts of the Age you are raiding
B
A fixed list written for each Age, worked through in order
Every save meets the same demands.
C
Drawn only from artifacts you have already seen in a castle
The handoff asks for it per Age; random draws keep each run different with no extra writing.
spoils
On a hunted raid, how are the spoils taken?
A
The Ophan takes them at the portal as you leave
You watch it happen.

choices.caption: The take, already animated: the lower wings sweep forward at 0.9 s.

choices: B
The haul vanishes from the Lair when you get back
The loss is seen in the raid, not discovered later.

wrapup.summary: A plan to put the Wick and the Ophan of Hours into raids, in three pieces, each its own pull request into the staging-2026-10-11 branch with tests, a co-op check and screenshots I have looked at.
wrapup.changing: The Lantern Warden gains a true form whose catch kills; a Lantern Warden in human form can no longer be killed; hunted raids bring the Ophan; the debt and the Collector give way to the Ophan's artifact demand.
wrapup.blocking: Your six picks. The Wick piece needs only the build order and the extra guards. The other four (the Ophan's arrival and speed, where artifacts are placed, how each demand is chosen, and how the spoils are taken) can wait until the Wick piece is built.
wrapup.next: On approval I log it, build the Wick piece, and show you before-and-after screenshots from a co-op run before opening its pull request.
